title: Make Number of Distinct Characters Equal
summary: Given two strings, word1 and word2, determine if it's possible to make the number of distinct characters in both strings equal by performing exactly one swap between a character in word1 and a character in word2.
statement: Given two strings, word1 and word2, determine if it's possible to make the number of distinct characters in both strings equal by performing exactly one swap between a character in word1 and a character in word2.
constraints: Perform exactly one swap between one character position in each nonempty word.
After the swap, compare the numbers of distinct characters in the two words.
Return whether some allowed swap makes those counts equal.
hints: Only character frequencies matter, not the positions selected.
Try every distinct character present in the first word against every distinct character in the second.
For different characters, a distinct count falls only when the removed frequency was one and rises only when the received character was absent.
The alphabet is bounded, so enumerating frequency-map keys covers every positional swap while avoiding repeated equivalent work.

tests.explanation: Any swap leaves the first word with two distinct characters and the second with one.
Swapping c from the first word with a from the second leaves two distinct characters in each.
